records.title: Subatmospheric Decompression Sickness in Man
records.locator: Printed pp. 130–134 (PDF pp. 127–131), neurological case numbers 17 and 18
records.note: These are numbered neurological cases. Fryer's fatality table uses different numbering. The same report already supplies source-defined aggregate observations and a separately indexed case 28.

observations.outcome_window: During the chamber exposure through recovery. Delayed visual, motor and cognitive signs followed descent.
observations.locator: Fryer 1969, printed pp. 130–131 (PDF pp. 127–128), neurological Case 17
observations.note: The source cites Roxburgh 1953 for this historical case. Early hand spasms occurred during the hypoxia demonstration. Approximate delay to the later neurological phase is recorded separately. The author reports hospitalization, seizure and later neurological recovery.
observations.protocol: Farnborough. A 34-year-old pilot had an initial hypoxia demonstration at 28,000 ft. Oxygen was resumed and joint pain was recorded on ascent through 32,000 ft. Maximum pressure altitude is unavailable.

milestones.name: acute_hypoxia_demonstration
milestones.note: Hand spasms and deteriorating writing during the unsupplemented hypoxia demonstration. Oxygen was then resumed.

milestones.name: joint_pain_during_ascent
milestones.note: Approximately three minutes after oxygen was first given. Bilateral arm tingling was followed by pain in multiple joints.

milestones.name: loss_of_consciousness
milestones.note: Just over one minute after the joint pain, the report describes pallor, increasing sweating and loss of consciousness. The maximum altitude is unstated.

milestones.name: consciousness_returns_during_descent
milestones.note: On regaining consciousness, the pilot reported right-arm weakness and tingling.

milestones.name: right_arm_tingling_clears
milestones.note: Approximate retrospective estimate. Power had begun returning on descent.

milestones.name: delayed_neurological_deterioration
milestones.note: Approximate and uncertain. Visual deterioration preceded headache, vomiting and loss of fine control.

milestones.name: hospital_seizure
milestones.note: A generalized seizure was witnessed during examination the following morning.

milestones.name: right_parietal_eeg_finding
milestones.note: The report describes a focal low-frequency right parietal EEG abnormality.

milestones.name: eeg_normalization_and_discharge
milestones.note: Approximate interval to EEG normalization and discharge, with unclear starting point. The report subsequently notes return to duty.

observations.outcome_window: During chamber ascent and descent through hospital recovery. The first witnessed generalized seizure occurred on the following evening.
observations.locator: Fryer 1969, printed pp. 131–134 (PDF pp. 128–131), neurological Case 18
observations.note: Fryer describes a case he observed. Acute hypoxia was part of the training, followed by pain and delayed neurological deterioration. The source reports a probable decompression relationship and eventual complete recovery.
observations.protocol: A 33-year-old pilot took part in a training chamber demonstration including 25,000 ft followed by 37,000 ft. The report describes two earlier uneventful demonstrations.

milestones.name: training_start
milestones.note: 23 September 1957. Mental impairment occurred during the initial 25,000-ft hypoxia demonstration.

milestones.name: upper_stage_symptoms_chamber_operator_timing
milestones.note: Chamber operator's estimate. The pilot stopped writing and appeared dazed. Knee pain and visual blurring were also reported at this stage.

milestones.name: upper_stage_symptoms_medical_officer_timing
milestones.note: Medical officer's estimate of the same interval as the operator's 30-second estimate.

milestones.name: post_training_symptoms
milestones.note: Light-headedness and frontal headache were reported at exit. The pilot later recalled nausea, groin pain and weak knees at that time.

milestones.name: next_day_medical_assessment
milestones.note: 24 September. The medical officer did not initially know about the chamber exposure and suspected influenza.

milestones.name: first_witnessed_generalized_seizure
milestones.note: 24 September. Later seizures were observed by the doctor and in hospital.

milestones.name: hospital_specialist_assessment
milestones.note: 24 September. The pilot was alert but amnesic after further seizure activity.

milestones.name: abnormal_eeg
milestones.note: Source's fourth-day count. The EEG abnormality was interpreted as possibly embolic.

milestones.name: normal_repeat_eeg
milestones.note: The report describes progressive complete recovery and normal repeat EEG.
